newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - MAY 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - MAY 15.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The current general director of Zivnostenska Banka and the president of the Banking Association, Jiri Kunert, is putting himself forward as a candidate for the highest post at Komercni Banka.
- In connection to an investigation into the causes of the insolvency of Kreditni Banka Plzen, another seven people were accused by the police of fraud.

- Of the four largest domestic banks, Komercni Banka had the largest net profits during the first quarter of this year, 867.8 million crowns. Ceska Sporitelna had 632.2 million crowns, followed by Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka with 577.4 million crowns and Investicni a Postovni Banka with 427.1 million crowns.
- British Midland Bank, which obtained a licence last year for banking on the domestic market, opened its Prague branch.

LIDOVE NOVINY - According to a survey from IVVM, the opposition Social Democrats (CSSD) are ahead of the Civic Democratic Party (ODS) in the polls with 25 percent, an increase of two percent. ODS is at an all time low of 18 percent, the Christian Democrats (KDU-CSL) at 14.5 percent and the Civic Democratic Union (ODA) at 10 percent.

- By tomorrow at the latest, the two most indebted hospitals, Motol and General Faculty, should begin paying their debts to creditors. Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik signed a contract with Konsolidacni Banka to issue credits to the hospitals.
- According to the director of Moravia Steel, the majority owner of AB Barrandov film studios, freezing Barrandov's property is not a threat to film production.
- In July, the World Trade Organisation will evaluate the compatibility of the Czech Republic's import deposit system with international orders, taking into account the state of the Czech economy.

- By the beginning of the summer holidays, the first steps in the technological processes for renewing production in Poldi Steel should begin. This was decided on yesterday by all participating sides at a meeting at the Industry and Trade Ministry.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - The cabinet approved the proposal for housing loans of 200,000 crowns yesterday. Contrary to the original proposal, which would provide the loans for flats of up to 70 square metres, even citizens who want to build larger flats can receive loans.
- According to a decision from the cabinet yesterday, social security will increase by five percent from July.
- Shareholders of Favorit Rokycany approved a decrease in basic capital yesterday by 40 percent to 52.84 million crowns to cover losses from between 1993 and 1995.
- Until the end of this July, importers will be allowed to bring a maximum of 1,500 tonnes of fresh apples into the Czech Republic, according to the cabinet's decision.
- The new law on waste approved by the cabinet on Tuesday does not coincide with EU regulations and the Environment Ministry estimates that it will propose another law around the year 2000.

- Parliament will reach a decision in one week on the amount of commercials on Czech public television and how much citizens will have to pay for its operation. Yesterday's discussions in parliament showed that these two questions are still open.
PRAVO - The cabinet privatisation committee will decide on the privatisation of 73 percent of shares of Crystalex Novy Bor on Monday.
- On Friday, the forced administrator of Agrobanka, Jiri Klumpar, will announce the three candidates chosen to buy the healthy part of the bank.
- Sazka a.s. put revenue into its account at the Education, Youth and Sports Ministry of 681 million crowns, which is the largest amount ever for the lottery and gambling company.

- On the basis of an exception from the Security Council of the the U.N., Zetor once again began exporting to Iraq. The company also decided to increase its basic capital this year to 4.139 billion crowns from 453 million.
-- Prague Newsroom, 420-2-2423-0003
